text.p: Finnish bank Alandsbanken AB said in a statement on Friday it expected net income from financial operations to fall this year, but earnings would nevertheless be satisfactory.
"Pressure on margins and still lower interest rates than in 1996 are expected to reduce net income from financial operations during 1997," it said.
Wage costs would remain at last year's level while credit losses would fall, it said.
"Overall, this should lead to satisfactory earnings in 1997 as well," the bank added.

In 1996, group operating profit after credit losses rose 5.6 percent to 48.5 million markka. Net income from financial operations edged 1.9 percent higher to 115.4 million markka. Credit losses fell 21 percent to 15.0 million markka.
